newsitem.title: USA: Schering-Plough buys Mallinckrodt unit for $405 million.
newsitem.headline: Schering-Plough buys Mallinckrodt unit for $405 million.

text.p: Schering-Plough Corp. said Monday it agreed to acquire Mallinckrodt Inc.'s worldwide animal health business for $405 million in cash.

Schering-Plough said the Mallinckrodt unit will be integrated into its Schering-Plough Animal Health subsidiary to form the world's sixth-largest animal health business, with annual sales of about $650 million.

Schering-Plough, which is based in Madison, N.J., said the acquisition of Mallinckrodt Veterinary Inc., which had 1996 sales of $456 million, should have a positive impact on its earnings next year and beyond.

It said the acquisition will broaden Schering-Plough Animal Health's product lines, expand geographic distribution, add new research technologies and products in development and generate sufficient cash flow and profits to internally fund competitive R&D levels.

Schering-Plough, a research-based pharmaceutical and health products company, said the combined organisation will compete in a $10 billion worldwide animal health market, excluding the nutritional and feed additive segment.
The acquisition will strengthen Scherling's position in the United States and Europe and give it an effective presence in Latin America and the Pacific Rim.

It said Mallinckrodt Veterinary's product lines complement Schering-Plough Animal Health's portfolio, notably in parasiticides, growth promotants and in offering a broader biologicals line for pets, livestock and poultry.

St. Louis-based Mallinckrodt is a major producer of diagnostic imaging agents, medical devices, pain relief pharmaceuticals, catalysts and laboratory and microelectronic chemicals. It had net sales of $2.2 billion last year.
Schering-Plough's stock lost 37.5 cents to $86.125 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange while Mallinckrodt added 25 cents to $36.375, also on the NYSE.
